result.summary: The high and medium findings are not fixed in the shipped icons. All of them (sample_and_hold and voltage_controlled_amplifier high; opamp, pid_regulator, pal_chip and oscillator_chip medium) are faults in the frozen kit CHIP_FACES table. The orchestrator's job decision and STYLE.md line 256 both say chips stay one-line chip_icon(id) modules, with no hand-drawn or chip()-based workarounds, so every correction goes to kit_requests below. I checked each proposed face myself with kit.chip.place_face and rendered previews to /tmp/claude-1000/-home-svein-dev-ElectricalAge/4df54121-69c8-45b9-bb04-77f6b30797c5/scratchpad/proposals.png. In that preview the sample_and_hold inner tick is hard to see even at 4x and has not been checked at GUI 2. I also checked analogchips.png zoomed in: the sample_and_hold tile is a triangle with an inner tick and a green caret, and the VCA tile prints the text 'VCA'. So both MATCH breaks are real and still present in the shipped icons. signal_processor (the only icon edited) got the cheap low fixes. The opening is now 6x8 (cols 6..11, rows 5..12) with a 1 px white rim on all four sides, matching the model's even rx frame. The inner left jamb is WHITE_PLASTIC[1] as STYLE §3 asks. The cabinet white is frozen as WHITE_PLASTIC (IRON[1..5], no new colours) in families/chips.py. The build passes: 22 built with --strict, 0 failed, 0 warnings. The contact sheet was regenerated and checked at GUI 2, GUI 3, on the dark panel and in the CVD rows: logic and analog chips stay apart, and signal_processor reads as a white cabinet with lit LEDs.

result.summary:
I revised the chips set: all 22 ids build with build.py --strict (22/22 ok), and the contact sheet is regenerated and checked at GUI 2 and zoomed. Every high and medium issue is fixed, and so are the cheap low ones:
- **schmitt_trigger_chip:** now a bare hysteresis loop in the hue, no longer the closed INK square inside a triangle.
- **amplifier:** now has one input.
- **voltage_controlled_amplifier:** one input plus an INK control lead from the top that lands on the slope.
- **opamp:** the signs moved to rows 11 and 17 and sit level with their leads. The reviewer's untested row-10 '-' turned out to touch the slope, and row 11 is clean.
- **oscillator_chip:** now voltage-controlled, like its siblings.
- **Six logic gates:** now have 3 inputs on rows 10/15/20, chosen so the outer leads join the curved OR/XOR back on both rows.
- **signal_processor:** the outer leads moved to rows 10 and 20.

The new drawings live as helpers in families/chips.py, and the kit is untouched. Several fixes depart from the literal STYLE 9 rows, so the orchestrator needs to amend STYLE 9 (listed in open_questions). The 4 kit_requests cover the same helpers.

result.summary:
I revised all 18 power_passive icons from the review; the --strict build passes with 0 warnings and the contact sheet is regenerated. I checked it at GUI-2 on light and dark backgrounds and in the CVD rows.

High-severity fixes:
- **Diode trio:** the can now sits between the walls, with both walls repainted over it. The 1 px band is the brightest feature and is clear of the wall face. The digits are dim RUBBER_BLACK[5] at gap 1, so '10' and '25' read with the band rather than as '10f'. The cost is a bracket 1 px wider than the reference, because '25' plus a separated band can't fit 7 columns. This is listed as an open question.
- **large_rheostat:** redrawn as a castellated heatsink. The back fins notch the silhouette, the tan coil is sunk between the fins and shows through 2 px front slots, and the fin and wall tops are lit so the block reads on dark backgrounds.

Medium-severity fixes:
- **dc_dc_converter:** a larger core loop with a 3x3 open window, and thin 2-row windings at different heights.
- **Resistor family:** CERAMIC is re-derived from #d4922c, at least 19.5 ΔE from every WOOD step, and now amber. Each body has two GOLD tabs on its top face.
- **rheostat:** a full-length red track with a small wiper block across it.
- **thermistor:** a legible '°C', clear of the outlines. The degree is one floating pixel because the 2x2 version touched the outline.
- **Fuse holder:** a round copper-threaded seat, and the leftover white pixels are gone.

Low-severity fixes:
- **power_capacitor_block and power_inductor_block:** the components now sit inside the cabinet opening.
- **power_inductor:** the stray lead pixel is gone.

The lead fuses are unchanged, waiting for the owner to rule on STYLE §8. The kit requests, manifest issues and open questions from the review are carried forward.

result.summary:
I fixed every high and medium review issue that the family files can fix, and the cheap low ones. The build passes --strict with no warnings for all 12 ids, and I regenerated and read the sheet, including the protan, deutan and tritan rows.

- **Relays (5 ids):** the cage interior is now the tier-tinted backplate seen through the glass (plate_ramp(t)[3]) instead of a dark CAV field. CAV is gone from the silhouette, and the frame is white S[4]. The copper coil runs the full width on a steel yoke so it never touches the tier field. I did this instead of the reviewer's recipe because no copper step is far enough from both the HV and VHV panes.
- **Lever switch (signal, LV, MV):** the hub is now an octagonal disc() with a white lever, and the contact plate shows only as two slotted ends. At GUI-2 it no longer reads as a '+'.
- **LED switch:** a square 12x12 plate with a dark recess and a lit lip, holding a white push-button cube with a 1 px lit LED.
- **Knife switch (HV, VHV):** the blades stay on the front face, and there are clip blocks at both ends of both bars.
- **Breaker:** a longer 12x6 case. The module has a blue band, a red stripe, and a 3x2 blue knob in its saddle with a flag.

Still open: signal vs LV under deutan is a kit-level cross-step collision (kit_requests 1 and 2), and the artist can't fix it within the file rules.

It now uses a TEMPORARY family shim, power_breaker in families/power_switching.py, built only from kit primitives (hline, line, contact, stroke). The shim draws no fixed-contact dot, centres the cross on the fixed-contact point (cols 19..26, rows 13..20), sets the blade tip at (14,6) and runs the right lead out of the cross (cols 25..27). result.summary: I revised power_switching after the review. All 12 ids pass build.py --strict (12/12, exit 0), and I regenerated and checked the contact sheet with the CVD rows. Fixes: (1) electrical_breaker now uses a temporary family shim, built from kit primitives, that leaves out the fixed-contact dot and centres the cross. It now reads clearly as a breaker cross at GUI 2 and on the dark row. It should go back to kit breaker() once the kit request lands. (2) signal_cable_switch now shows signal_cable's routed step with the switch cut into the run (the reviewer's preferred direction, with the V opened). It is marked PROVISIONAL pending the owner's choice, and the legs-down alternative is kept as a one-line swap. The low-severity relay coil hole is left to the kit (kit request with a verified fix) rather than forking the binding relay() convention. The CVD sibling overlaps wait on the palette decision. The other 10 icons are unchanged and follow STYLE 8.6 exactly.
